quotes.text: The Sessions Court conducted the trial and after appreciating the evidence on record, convicted the appellants for the said offences and sentenced them to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs. 2,000/- each for the offences under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC, and to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- each for the offences under Section 306 read with Section 34 of IPC.
The High Court confirmed the said conviction and sentence as per the impugned order.
Conviction of the appellants u/s.498A upheld, however they are acquitted from the charges levelled u/s.306 by giving them benefit of doubt

neutral_facts.value: The deceased, a woman, married one of the accused approximately three years prior to the incident. The accused, who were the deceased's in-laws, were alleged to have subjected her to physical and mental harassment due to dowry demands. The deceased was found dead in a well, and the prosecution alleged that the accused had harassed her to the point of suicide. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the deceased's parents and uncle, as well as a neighbor, to establish the harassment. However, the evidence did not conclusively show that the accused had instigated or aided the deceased in committing suicide. The post-mortem report indicated the cause of death was drowning due to asphyxia, but there was no evidence to determine whether the death was accidental or suicidal. The prosecution failed to establish that the accused had abetted the deceased's suicide, despite the harassment allegations.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to adduce any clinching evidence to conclude that the appellants abetted the deceased to commit suicide, and that mere commission of suicide would not be sufficient for the court to raise the presumption under Section 113A of the Evidence Act.

quotes.text: However, it failed to adduce any clinching evidence to conclude that the appellants abetted the deceased to commit suicide
Mere fact of commission of suicide by itself would not be sufficient for the court to raise the presumption u/s.113A, Evidence Act, and to hold the accused guilty of s.306

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for conviction under Section 306 IPC, there must be evidence of instigation, conspiracy, or intentional aid by the accused, and that the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused abetted the suicide.

quotes.text: In order to convict a person for the offences u/s.306, the basic constituents of the offence namely where the death was suicidal and whether there was an abetment on the part of the accused as contemplated in s.107 have to be established
For proving the charge u/s.306, also there has to be an evidence with regard to the positive act on the part of the accused to instigate or aid to drive a person to commit suicide

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the conviction under Section 498A was upheld, but the appellants were acquitted of the charges under Section 306 due to lack of satisfactory evidence. The appellants had already served two years of imprisonment for the Section 498A conviction, so they were set free.

quotes.text: In absence of any satisfactory evidence on record, both the Courts below committed grave error in holding the appellants guilty of the offence u/s.306
Since the appellants have already undergone the imprisonment for two years for the offence u/s.498A r/w s.34, as directed by the courts below, to be set free forthwith
